title: Trails of Central Asia | Uncover Kazakhstan & Uzbekistan
highlights: Uncover Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan’s blend of vast steppes, ancient cities, and vibrant cultures—offering a unique journey through Central Asia’s historic crossroads.
Explore Khodjand Fortress, known for its massive walls and rich history as a key Silk Road defense, offering insight into Tajikistan’s past and strategic importance.
Walk through Shah-i-Zinda, a sacred Samarkand necropolis famed for its vibrant tilework and centuries-old mausoleums, reflecting artistic heritage.
Discover Burabay National Park, famed for its stunning lakes, unique rock formations, and rich wildlife—a peaceful escape blending nature and culture in Kazakhstan.
Visit Charyn Canyon, famed for its towering red rock formations and rugged landscapes—often called Kazakhstan’s Grand Canyon for its breathtaking views.
overview: Start your adventure in Tashkent with a city walking tour, exploring its vibrant streets and historic sites. Next, head to Khujand, Tajikistan, where you’ll discover ancient fortresses, cultural landmarks, and bustling bazaars. Then, transfer to Samarkand to visit iconic places like Registan Square, Gur-e-Amir Mausoleum, and Shah-i-Zinda. Journey to the Seven Lakes in Tajikistan’s Fann Mountains, enjoying stunning landscapes and local village life. Return to Tashkent for some leisure time before flying to Astana to explore its futuristic architecture and nearby Burabay National Park’s natural beauty. Fly to Almaty for city highlights and experience the Medeu Ice Skating Rink and Shymbulak Ski Resort. Finally, take a day trip to Charyn Canyon and Kolsai Lake, known for dramatic rock formations and pristine alpine lakes, before your departure.

know_before_you_go: Check visa rules for Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan; some nationalities require visas in advance.
Uzbekistan uses the Uzbek som; Kazakhstan uses the Kazakhstan tenge. Carry some cash, as cards may not be widely accepted.
Dress modestly when visiting mosques and religious sites.
Internet access can be limited in remote areas. Plan accordingly.
Uzbek and kazakh are official languages; Russian is widely spoken. English may be limited outside major cities.
The region is generally safe for tourists but always follow local advice and keep valuables secure.
Some excursions involve moderate walking and altitude changes (Seven Lakes, Burabay, Charyn Canyon).

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Tashkent | Tashkent Walking Tour
days.desc: Welcome to Tashkent! Upon arrival at the airport, get driven to your hotel. Check in and rest for some time. From hotel, begin your walking tour in Amir Temur Square, where locals gather near the statue of Uzbekistan’s most iconic leader. Head to Broadway Alley, lined with painters, snack stalls, and weekend musicians. Nearby, the Alisher Navoiy Theater stands proud, hosting classic operas and modern shows. Conclude your tour at Chorsu Bazaar, where every corner bursts with color and spices.

days.title: Trip to Khujand, Tajikistan
days.desc: Today, set off to Khujand, a historic city once rebuilt by Alexander the Great. Visit Khudjant Palace, inspired by St. Petersburg’s Petergof, known for its ornate halls. Next, walk through Khodjand Fortress and explore its archaeology museum with ancient regional artifacts. See the Mosque and Mausoleum of Sheikh Muslihiddin, a spiritual landmark, and the 19th-century Orthodox Church of Mary Magdalene. Conclude your day at Panjshanbe Bazaar, filled with local life, food, and crafts.

days.title: Transfer to Samarkand | Samarkand Walking Tour
days.desc: Post check out, get driven to Samarkand. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and rest. Later, get transferred to Gur-i Amir Сomplex for your walking tour. Begin at Registan Square, where the mosaic-covered madrasahs echo stories of past. Next, head to Gur-e-Amir, the final resting place of Timur, and learn about his legacy. Afterward, walk the quiet path of Shah-i-Zinda, where each mausoleum tells its own sacred tale. Conclude your walk at Siyob Bazaar, where locals gather for produce & sweets.

items.title: Amir Temur Mausoleum Gur-i Amir Сomplex

days.title: Tajikistan Seven Lakes Tour
days.desc: Today, take a scenic drive into Tajikistan’s Fann Mountains to explore the Seven Lakes. Begin at Nezhigon, where the water shifts color with the sun. Continue to Soya and Hushyor, quiet lakes nestled among steep hills. At Marguzor, the largest lake of the 7 lakes, enjoy a walk and listen to local stories. Afterward, meet villagers living close to nature, offering insight into mountain life. This trip blends stunning views with simple moments, giving you an experience of the region’s beauty.

days.title: Transfer to Tashkent | Leisure Time
days.desc: Post check out, get driven to Tashkent. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and spend your time at leisure. You can explore the State Museum of the Temurids to dive into the rich history of the Timurid Empire with its rare artifacts and exhibits. You can also visit the Tashkent Television Tower, a towering symbol of modern Uzbekistan offering panoramic city views. You can discover Besh Qozon Pilaf Center, famous for its Uzbek pilaf, where tradition meets flavor in a unique dining experience.

days.title: Fly to Astana | Astana Sightseeing Tour
days.desc:
Post check out, get driven to the airport for your flight to Astana. Upon arrival at 
Nursultan Nazarbayev International Airport, get transferred to your hotel. Check in and rest. Visit Baiterek Tower, a symbol of Kazakhstan’s independence with stunning views from its golden sphere. Next, step inside the Nur-Alem Sphere, the world’s largest spherical building and legacy of Expo 2017, showcasing future energy. Afterward, explore Khan Shatyr, a transparent tent with shops, dining and even a beach.

days.title: Trip to Burabay National Park
days.desc: Take a day trip to Burabay National Park, known for its lakes, forests, and granite hills. Just a few hours from Astana, this park is a peaceful retreat from the city. Walk along Lake Borovoe, surrounded by pine-covered slopes, and spot rock formations shaped by wind and time. Visit Zhumbaktas Rock and climb to hilltop viewpoints for wide views of the steppe. Locals call it the "Kazakh Switzerland" for its mix of nature and legends. It's a quiet place where fresh air and scenery meet.

days.title: Fly to Almaty | Almaty City Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Post check out, get transferred to the airport for your flight to Almaty. Upon arrival at Almaty International Airport, get driven to your hotel. Check in & rest. Later, explore the city. Begin at Almaty’s Monument of Independence, where the golden figure atop a tall pillar marks Kazakhstan’s journey to nationhood. Walk to the nearby Park of 28 Panfilov Guardsmen, a peaceful space honoring soldiers who defended Moscow in WWII. Discover Ascension Cathedral, a wooden structure built without nails.

days.title: Day Trip to Medeu Ice Skating Rink & Shymbulak Ski Resort
days.desc: Take a day trip from Almaty to two major mountain attractions. Start at Medeu Ice Skating Rink, the highest Olympic-sized rink in the world, where you can skate in a scenic mountain setting. Then ride the cable car up to Shymbulak Ski Resort, known for its wide slopes and modern facilities. Enjoy skiing, snowboarding, or a peaceful ride up the lifts with views of snow-covered peaks all around. It’s a day filled with fresh air and outdoor activity. Afterward, get driven back to your hotel.

items.title: Day Trip to Medeu Ice Skating Rink & Shymbulak Ski Resort

days.title: Day Trip to Charyn Canyon and Kolsai Lake From Almaty
days.desc: Take a day trip from Almaty to two stunning natural landmarks. Begin at Charyn Canyon, often called "Kazakhstan’s Grand Canyon," where deep red cliffs and rock formations line the river valley—perfect for hiking and photography. Continue to Kolsai Lake, the largest of three alpine lakes nestled in forested mountains, reached via a scenic trail. Walk along the shore or hike nearby to enjoy the pristine clear water and pine-scented air. It’s a refreshing journey into wild landscapes.

items.title: Day Trip to Charyn Canyon and Kolsai Lake From Almaty

days.title: Departure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out and get driven to the airport for your flight back home. This marks end of your Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan tour.
